title: Finite algebras over strict affinoids admit Tate quotient presentations
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $A\ne0$ be a commutative $K$-algebra admitting a surjective $K$-algebra map $K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r\rangle\to A$ from the restricted-series ring [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. Let $B\ne0$ be a commutative unital $A$-algebra which is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; its $K$-algebra structure is the composite through $A$. There exist $m\ge0$ and a surjective $K$-algebra homomorphism $q:K\langle Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\rangle\to B$ such that $\|b\|_q=\inf_{q(f)=b}\|f\|_G$ is a complete nonarchimedean submultiplicative $K$-algebra norm on $B$, with $\|\lambda b\|_q=|\lambda|\|b\|_q$. Thus $B$ has an affinoid quotient presentation in the sense of [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. No injectivity of $A\to B$, reducedness, or separability is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 1.2.6(3), printed p.6 (PDF p.6), with the quotient-norm construction immediately preceding Exercise 1.2.4, printed pp.5–6. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Write $T=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r\rangle$ and let $\alpha:T\twoheadrightarrow A$ be the given map. Choose $A$-module generators $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ of $B$ using [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. They also generate $B$ as an $A$-algebra, since every element is already an $A$-linear combination of them. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], for each $i$ choose a monic relation $b_i^{d_i}+\sum_{j<d_i}u_{ij}b_i^j=0$, with $u_{ij}\in A$. Here $d_i\ge1$: a degree-zero monic relation would assert $1=0$ in the nonzero ring $B$. Lift each $u_{ij}$ to $v_{ij}\in T$ by surjectivity of $\alpha$. No lift of a ring homomorphism or injectivity of $A\to B$ is required.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral); finite-module generators and coefficient lifting.

proof.text: All $\|v_{ij}\|_G$ are finite by [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion]. Choose $\pi\in K$ with $0<|\pi|<1$, possible by nontriviality of the absolute value (invert an element of absolute value greater than one if necessary). For each $i$ choose $N_i\ge0$ large enough that $|\pi|^{N_i(d_i-j)}\|v_{ij}\|_G\le1$ for every $j<d_i$, and put $c_i=\pi^{N_i}$, $e_i=c_ib_i$, $a_{ij}=c_i^{d_i-j}v_{ij}$. The choice exists because there are finitely many positive exponents $d_i-j$ and $|\pi|^N\to0$. Coefficientwise scaling gives $\|a_{ij}\|_G\le1$. Multiplying the relation of step 1 by $c_i^{d_i}$ yields $e_i^{d_i}+\sum_{j<d_i}\alpha(a_{ij})e_i^j=0$. Since $c_i$ is a nonzero scalar, $b_i=c_i^{-1}e_i$, so the $e_i$ still generate $B$ over $A$.

source.place: Agent scaling argument for the finite-algebra assertion of Conrad Theorem 1.2.6(3); coefficient Gauss norms as in Bosch section 1.2.

proof.text: Set $P=T[Y_1,\ldots,Y_s]$, $D=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r,Y_1,\ldots,Y_s\rangle$ and $f_i=Y_i^{d_i}+\sum_{j<d_i}a_{ij}Y_i^j$. The polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] gives evaluation $P\to B$ through $\alpha$ and $Y_i\mapsto e_i$. It is surjective: lift the finitely many $A$-coefficients in any linear combination of the $e_i$ to $T$. The relations of step 2 vanish under this map, so it factors through a surjection $P/(f_i)\to B$; explicitly two representatives differing by $\sum h_if_i$ have the same evaluation. Apply [lem-trf-tate-separated-monic-quotient], whose hypotheses $d_i\ge1$, separate $Y_i$ dependence, and coefficient norms at most one were verified in steps 1–2. Its canonical isomorphism $P/(f_i)\simeq D/(f_i)$ gives a surjection $q:D\twoheadrightarrow B$ by composing the quotient map, the inverse isomorphism, and evaluation. It is a $K$-algebra map by construction. Set $m=r+s$.

source.place: Section 1.2 Theorem 8 and Proposition 14 proof; separate-monic quotient comparison followed by evaluation.

proof.text: Put $I=\ker(q)$. The fibres of $q$ are exactly the cosets of $I$, so $D/I\to B$, $f+I\mapsto q(f)$, is a bijective $K$-algebra homomorphism. By [lem-trf-tate-ideal-best-approximation], the infimum of the Gauss norms in every coset of $I$ is attained. In particular, $I$ is closed: if $f$ is a limit of elements of $I$, its distance to $I$ is zero, and a minimizing $g\in I$ satisfies $\|f-g\|_G=0$, hence $f=g\in I$. The algebra $D$ has a complete submultiplicative norm by [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion]; its scalar equality follows directly from the coefficient supremum. Thus [lem-trf-banach-closed-ideal-quotient] applies to $R=D$ and this closed ideal $I$. Transfer its complete submultiplicative homogeneous quotient norm through the displayed bijection. Since $q^{-1}(q(f))=f+I$, its formula is exactly $\|b\|_q=\inf_{q(f)=b}\|f\|_G$ required in the statement.

source.place: Section 1.3 Corollary 9 and section 1.4 Proposition 4(i)–(iii), printed pp.21 and 23; generic quotient completeness supplied by Mathlib.

proof.text: For $b,b'\in B$, choose minimizing representatives $f,f'\in D$ by [lem-trf-tate-ideal-best-approximation]. Then $q(f+f')=b+b'$ and the Gauss maximum bound of [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] gives $\|b+b'\|_q\le\|f+f'\|_G\le\max(\|f\|_G,\|f'\|_G)=\max(\|b\|_q,\|b'\|_q)$. This proves the additional nonarchimedean inequality. Also $\|1\|_q\le\|1\|_G=1$, while $B\ne0$ and submultiplicativity give $0<\|1\|_q\le\|1\|_q^2$, so $\|1\|_q=1$. All clauses of an affinoid quotient presentation [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation] now hold for $q$. The construction applies to nonreduced algebras and noninjective structure maps; it uses only the finite-module hypothesis and the assumed nonzero rings.

source.place: Section 1.4 Proposition 4, explicit maximum-inequality and unit checks from minimizing representatives.
